rule: A (anticipates): the action starts when the sentence ends, then >= 2 s with an empty band. D (describes): the action is already on screen, still, >= 0.5 s before the sentence. Each sentence max(3 s, words/1.8 + 1.0 s). The camera arrives before the sentence.

phrases.text: One real run of my experiment. The ticket: rename two fields in the order event.
Two other teams read these fields. The agent cannot see those teams.

phrases.moment: whole frame: scene and log, the log outlined
phrases.text: On the right: the real log of this run. On the left: an animation of that log.

phrases.moment: camera on Product and Maya, the architect
phrases.text: On the left of the office: product, and the architect.

phrases.moment: camera on the agent and the CI tower
phrases.text: In the middle: the code agent, on the orders team. Then the CI tower.

phrases.moment: camera behind the glass: billing, analytics, storefront
phrases.text: On the right, behind the glass: billing, analytics and the storefront.

phrases.moment: camera on Product, Maya, the agent and the CI tower; then the ticket flies to the agent and the ARCH-1…ARCH-8 sheet from Maya's library to the tower
phrases.text: Now product gives the ticket to the agent. The architect gives CI the eight architecture checks.
Now the agent reads the code and changes the two names.

phrases.moment: the agent own tests pass sign on screen
phrases.text: The tests in its own repo are green.
It opens a pull request.
CI is the only reviewer. It runs ten checks. Eight are for architecture.
Red. Rule ARCH-4: another team needs the old field.

phrases.moment: before Meanwhile: the camera goes behind the glass
phrases.text: Now look behind the glass, at the tests of the other teams.
Billing fails. Analytics fails. Billing cannot send the invoice.
The agent never sees these tests.

phrases.moment: before the red build reaches the agent
phrases.text: What goes back to the agent is only the red build.
The agent reads the message from CI, and fixes the code.
It keeps the old names as aliases, next to the new ones.
It sends the fix. CI runs again.
CI passes. Every check is good.
Before the repair: CI said no, and two teams broke. After: every team passes.
The agent did not need a meeting. It needed a red build.
